summary: PulseRx — mid-stream token interleaving from multiplexer misrouting causing garbled streaming completions and spike in billable tokens
description: Issue summary: During PulseRx's morning ingest window (09:30-10:15 UTC, 2026-03-11) a subset of streaming completions returned interleaved token sequences and occasionally duplicated segments from concurrent requests. This produced garbled patient-facing summaries and inflated token counts on billing. Impact: high — customer-facing clinical summarization pipeline produced invalid notes for ~0.9% of requests in the window, and PulseRx reports a ~22% increase in billable tokens for the same period.
impact: Customer-visible data corruption for real-time clinical summaries; temporary pause of production ingest by PulseRx for 35 minutes; billing spike and urgent executive escalation from the customer.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use PulseRx streaming endpoint with concurrency of 80+ short sessions (avg seq len 200 tokens). 2) Enable streaming with prefix caching and the default router policy. 3) Observe token interleaving when tests are run against us-east-1 serving pool while autoscaler is initiating node scale-up. Note: reproduced only with the exact concurrency and short TTL caching configuration.
logs: Representative log snippets attached as plain text in the ticket: 1) multiplexer debug: 'mux: session 0x8a3 collided with 0x9f1 on stream-id 43' 2) router: 'route fallback -> pool-b: raced req-id=...  timestamp mismatch' 3) billing: 'token-count raw 158 vs recorded 198 (dup tokens)'. Full log ranges: 2026-03-11T09:29:12Z - 2026-03-11T10:17:45Z (cut into diagnostics bundle).

2026-03-11 09:40 UTC - Support validated and escalated to SRE/Serving.
2026-03-11 09:52 UTC - SRE observed multiplexer collision patterns in serving-runtime; initiated traffic fencing to isolate affected GPU pool.
2026-03-11 10:01 UTC - Mitigation: route PulseRx traffic to a separate warm pool and temporarily disable prefix caching for their tenant.
2026-03-11 10:20 UTC - Customer re-enabled traffic; observed no further interleaving.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor or kernel-level preemption. After correlating mux debug traces with router events, we found a race in the internal multiplexer where per-connection stream IDs could be re-used by the same worker before KV cache flush completed. This condition is exacerbated during scale-up bursts when the autoscaler reassigns worker PIDs and the mux state machine does not fully quiesce. Evidence: sequence of events in mux trace shows overlapping stream-id windows and replayed token writes. Billing discrepancy arises from duplicated token emission logged by the encoder stage when the handler retried partial frames. Linked PRs address atomic tear-down of mux state and a defensive dedupe step in the encoder.
customer_communication:
- 2026-03-11 09:45 UTC: Acknowledged receipt and escalated; we communicated we were investigating and recommended pausing heavy ingest.
- 2026-03-11 10:15 UTC: Provided interim mitigation (traffic fencing + disable prefix caching) and ETA for a full fix.
- 2026-03-11 12:30 UTC: Confirmed temporary billing credit action and open reconciliation.
- 2026-03-14 12:00 UTC: Shared root cause summary, permanent fix timeline, and offered one month service credit for the impacted window. PulseRx accepted the credit and requested the post-incident report.
resolution: Permanent code fix (gh-5501) to the multiplexer state machine that ensures stream-id uniqueness during worker handover, plus an encoder-level dedup filter to drop repeated token frames mid-stream. Deployed to prod on 2026-03-14 11:30 UTC with a controlled rollout and 4-hour soak in us-east-1. Mitigations included tenant fencing and temporary prefix-cache disablement. Billing team issued a provisional credit for the affected window; reconciliation completed on 2026-03-13 with a final invoice adjustment.
follow_up_actions: 1) Postmortem doc created and published: confluence/redwood/incident-2026-03-11-pulserx-multiplexer. 2) Backport fix to 1.x maintenance branch and schedule canary (owner: Priya Natarajan, due 2026-03-20). 3) Add unit/integration tests around mux handover and stream-id lifecycle (owner: Serving QA). 4) Instrument an internal metric 'mux_stream_collision_rate' and alert at >0.1% per 15m (owner: SRE). 5) Billing pipeline to run daily reconciliation checks for unusual token deltas (owner: Finance Ops).
